stem: Which presentation is a classic clue to delayed bleeding due to factor XIII deficiency in a newborn?

options.text: Bleeding from the umbilical stump in a newborn
Haemarthrosis in a boy with family history

explanation: Bleeding from the umbilical stump in a newborn is the classic clue to factor XIII deficiency, which presents with delayed bleeding.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Correct because bleeding from the umbilical stump in a newborn is a classic neonatal presentation of factor XIII deficiency with delayed bleeding
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because epistaxis in an adolescent is more typical of mucocutaneous bleeding disorders such as von Willebrand disease or platelet dysfunction
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because haemarthrosis with a family history suggests haemophilia
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because easy bruising with previous DVT points towards dysfibrinogenaemia rather than factor XIII deficiency
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because bruising with an inconsistent history raises concern for non-accidental injury
